object_description: aligned volume enclosing a trapezoidal courtyard
design_condition: The new volume aligns with the neighboring buildings and forms a broad trapezoidal outdoor space between the addition and the historic buildings, while trees structure transversal connections and provide shading.

positive.statement: The reduced intervention within the historic area is appreciated.
New trees inside and outside the enclosure support spatial continuity and user orientation.
The tree arrangement along the southern edge is convincing environmentally and as a transition toward neighboring buildings.
The plants will provide effective long-term shading to the south-facing façade.
Managing evacuated water as a resource is a positive intention.
The idea of prefabricated wooden room cells is interesting.
The building envelope and system concept are clearly defined and generally satisfy the energy requirements.

negative.statement: The literal repetition of the historic structural guidelines is excessively formal.
Closing the sector with a secondary building weakens the generous perception of arrival into the common space.
The organization of external green spaces and new trees is fragmented and unresolved.
The transparent common living space is not well calibrated in shape, organization, or size.
The rigid arrangement of living cells creates poorly controlled spatial hierarchies.
Thermal breaks and external pillars create geometric complexity, thermal bridges, and difficult structural connections.
The potential interaction between the prefabricated cells and the remaining structure is not exploited.
Comfort and energy needs in the north-facing common spaces require verification.
The environmental sustainability of the materials is not addressed.
